currentContext.expansion: Rama Phosphates is running its largest expansion programme to date across three sites. At Udaipur it is expanding the SSP plant by 65,000 MTPA, which will take that unit's SSP capacity to 3,15,000 MTPA and lift the Company's overall SSP capacity to 9,79,000 MTPA; construction on this expansion, together with new greenfield GSSP/Granulation, Potassium Derived from Molasses (PDM) and Phosphate Rich Organic Manure (PROM) plants of 49,000 MTPA aggregate capacity at the same unit, started in 2026. At Dhule (Maharashtra), a greenfield SSP facility of 216,000 MTPA capacity, built on 54 acres of MIDC land acquired in 2022 with highly automated plant and machinery already purchased and Environmental Clearance received in 2023, is stated to be on track for commissioning by Q2 FY 2027; additional MgSO4, PDM/PROM and Urea-SSP plants are being introduced at the Dhule project, which management says will improve product availability and visibility, particularly for interior-market penetration. During FY 2026 the Company completed the Complex Fertilizer Urea-SSP plant at Indore of 1,02,950 MTPA - following the 74,000 MTPA Urea-SSP complex commissioned at Udaipur the previous year - taking overall Urea-SSP capacity to 176,950 MTPA, and installed a granulation machine at its micronutrient plant for granule-form products. It also extended the lease of the Nimbahera unit (66,000 MTPA, held on long-term lease) by five years to December 08, 2031. On the back of these projects management describes Rama as the third-largest SSP manufacturing capacity in India, against a total aggregate existing manufacturing capacity of 6.98 lakh MTPA across Indore, Udaipur, Nimbahera and Pune. No rupee capex quantum is disclosed anywhere in the routed text.
